title: Watercress Soup
subtitle: bright, peppery, and vivid green
excerpt: Watercress gives this soup its distinctive peppery bite and deep green colour. It cooks quickly so the colour stays bright. Leek and potato give body without heaviness. Serve warm or chilled as a light starter.
sourceNotes: A classic British spring soup. Watercress has been cultivated in Hampshire since the early 19th century. The chilled version has long been a favourite for dinner party starters.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the soup up to 24 hours ahead. Reheat gently or serve chilled.

content.text: Blend this soup as soon as it is cooked and serve straight away. The longer it sits, the duller the colour becomes. If using spinach instead of watercress, the flavour will be milder but the colour stays just as bright.

items.prepNote: use watercress -- or spinach as a substitute
white and pale green parts, sliced

content.text: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the leeks and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the potato and stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Add the watercress (or spinach). Cook for 2 minutes only.
Blend immediately until very smooth. Stir in the cream.
Season and serve at once, or chill quickly and serve cold.

items.cause: Overcooked before blending or left to sit
items.fix: Cook the watercress for no more than 2 minutes and blend immediately.

items.cause: Too much stock for the amount of potato
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for a few minutes to reduce, or add a little more cooked potato.

content.text: Watercress has been grown commercially in southern England since the 1800s. It was once sold by street vendors as a cheap, nutritious food for working people. This soup became popular as a refined starter in the 20th century. It works equally well as a chilled summer soup or a warm spring one.
